newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian Total index down, but bank shares up.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian Total index down, but bank shares up.

text.p: Banks outperformed the rest of the market on the Oslo Bourse on Tuesday, but the Total share index plunged with major European stock exchanges.

Oslo's Total index fell 0.94 percent to 1,089.52 points in heavy trade worth 1.4 billion crowns. A dealer said he expected the market, which has soared in the past three months, to be relatively quiet until after the Easter holidays.
The industry, shipping and insurance indexes all fell but the banking index edged up thanks to a rally by proposed merger partners Fokus Bank ASA and Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank).
BNbank ended 24 crowns higher at 191 crowns while Fokus gained a crown to finish at 59.50 crowns after Fokus proposed a merger with BNbank.

Most traded share at 385 million crowns was Norway's top commercial bank Den norske Bank (DnB) after two major blocks changed hands and the share ended 0.70 crowns lower at 29.30 crowns. Dealers said the trade in DnB was unrelated to BNbank and Fokus.
Among blue chips, industrial giant Norsk Hydro fell two crowns to 340 crowns.
